domain_symbols.science_model: physical, biological, chemical, and socioeconomic models
domain_symbols.field_or_state: fields, states, and ensemble quantities in scientific models

rules.name: Free energy seed
rules.input_form: partition-function ensemble data
preconditions: A canonical equilibrium ensemble and unit convention are fixed
rules.operation: Relate free energy to partition-function structure.
examples: Thermodynamic work potential is encoded through logarithmic partition-function data in equilibrium settings
counterexamples: Treating free energy as unrelated to the underlying ensemble model is invalid

rules.name: Electromagnetic wave seed
rules.input_form: source-free Maxwell field regime
preconditions: The standard homogeneous source-free regime is active
rules.operation: Derive electromagnetic wave propagation from Maxwell structure.
examples: Electromagnetic fields propagate dynamically rather than remaining static algebraic quantities
counterexamples: Discarding time dependence while still claiming wave propagation is invalid

rules.name: Gibbs measure seed
rules.input_form: energy levels and temperature scale
preconditions: A canonical statistical-mechanics setting is fixed
rules.operation: Assign Gibbs weights through exponential energy penalties normalized by the partition function.
examples: Higher-energy states are suppressed relative to lower-energy states according to the temperature scale
counterexamples: Assigning arbitrary unnormalized weights without ensemble structure is invalid

rules.name: Spacetime interval seed
rules.input_form: spacetime coordinates under an active metric convention
preconditions: A relativistic metric convention is fixed
rules.operation: Use metric structure to define invariant spacetime interval data.
examples: Coordinate changes may alter components while preserving interval-type invariant structure
counterexamples: Treating time and space as Euclidean coordinates under all relativistic transformations is invalid

rules.name: Reaction-diffusion seed
rules.input_form: coupled reacting and diffusing fields
preconditions: Reaction and diffusion mechanisms are fixed on a spatial domain
rules.operation: Model coupled local reaction and spatial diffusion dynamics.
examples: Pattern formation can arise from interplay between local reactions and spatial diffusion
counterexamples: Ignoring spatial coupling while claiming reaction-diffusion dynamics is invalid

rules.name: Chemical kinetics mass-action seed
rules.input_form: reaction network with stoichiometry
preconditions: A reaction network and rate constants are fixed
rules.operation: Build kinetic equations from stoichiometric reaction data under mass action.
examples: Nonlinear ODE systems in chemistry arise directly from reaction-network stoichiometry under mass action
counterexamples: Assigning arbitrary reaction exponents with no kinetic model justification is invalid

rules.name: Competitive equilibrium seed
rules.input_form: prices, allocations, and agent optimization data
preconditions: A standard competitive-market model is fixed
rules.operation: Recognize competitive equilibrium by joint individual optimality and market clearing.
examples: Equilibrium requires both individual optimality and aggregate consistency
counterexamples: Optimizing one agent in isolation does not determine market equilibrium

rules.name: Black-Scholes seed
rules.input_form: frictionless diffusion-based asset model and derivative claim
preconditions: The standard no-arbitrage diffusion assumptions hold
rules.operation: Model derivative valuation through the Black-Scholes-type pricing equation.
examples: No-arbitrage and diffusion assumptions lead to PDE-based option pricing structure
counterexamples: Applying Black-Scholes outside its modeling assumptions without adjustment is invalid

rules.name: Network diffusion seed
rules.input_form: graph-based population with interaction or threshold dynamics
preconditions: A graph or interaction network and update rule are fixed
rules.operation: Model spread or adoption through network-coupled state evolution.
examples: Adoption patterns can depend on local neighborhood state rather than on isolated individual parameters alone
counterexamples: Treating population interactions as completely structure-free loses the network model

rules.name: Signal detection seed
rules.input_form: latent signal-noise model with response threshold or psychometric data
preconditions: A probabilistic response model and discrimination setting are fixed
rules.operation: Model decision behavior through signal-noise separation or psychometric transition structure.
examples: Response accuracy can vary systematically with signal strength rather than as an unstructured yes-no outcome
counterexamples: Ignoring latent uncertainty while claiming a signal-detection model is invalid

rules.name: Entropy production seed
rules.input_form: irreversible process model with entropy accounting
preconditions: A standard irreversible-process interpretation and entropy balance are fixed
rules.operation: Impose nonnegative entropy production in the standard nonequilibrium setting.
examples: Dissipation distinguishes irreversible evolution from ideal reversible balance laws
counterexamples: Assigning negative total entropy production in a closed irreversible model is invalid in the standard setting

rules.name: Poynting flux seed
rules.input_form: electromagnetic field configuration with energy-balance interpretation
preconditions: A Maxwell-type field model with energy accounting is fixed
rules.operation: Encode electromagnetic energy transport through Poynting-flux balance.
examples: Wave propagation carries energy through space rather than only oscillating local field values
counterexamples: Treating electromagnetic energy as present with no transport structure is invalid in the standard flux setting

rules.name: FLRW symmetry seed
rules.input_form: homogeneous and isotropic cosmological spacetime model
preconditions: Homogeneity, isotropy, and an FLRW-type metric ansatz are fixed
rules.operation: Reduce cosmological relativistic structure to scale-factor dynamics under FLRW symmetry.
examples: Large-scale symmetry assumptions compress relativistic geometry into a small number of dynamical cosmological variables
counterexamples: Arbitrary anisotropic or inhomogeneous universes are not automatically FLRW models

rules.name: Friedmann expansion seed
rules.input_form: cosmological scale factor with curvature and energy-density data
preconditions: An FLRW-type cosmological model and matter-energy content are fixed
rules.operation: Relate cosmic expansion to curvature and matter-energy content through a Friedmann-type equation.
examples: Cosmological dynamics are encoded through scale-factor evolution rather than by static spatial geometry alone
counterexamples: Assuming cosmic expansion is independent of matter-energy content is invalid in the standard Friedmann setting

rules.name: Virial balance seed
rules.input_form: gravitationally bound astrophysical system under an averaging regime
preconditions: A bound astrophysical system and averaging assumptions are fixed
rules.operation: Constrain bulk astrophysical behavior through averaged kinetic-potential balance.
examples: Cluster or stellar-system scale estimates can be constrained through bulk balance instead of exact trajectory tracking for every constituent
counterexamples: Arbitrary nonequilibrium transients do not automatically satisfy virial balance identities without the required averaging regime

rules.name: SIR compartment seed
rules.input_form: population state partitioned into susceptible, infectious, and removed classes
preconditions: A compartment model and transmission/removal conventions are fixed
rules.operation: Model epidemiological evolution through coupled SIR state transfers.
examples: Outbreak growth and decline can be modeled by state transfers between population compartments rather than by one scalar trend alone
counterexamples: Ignoring interaction-driven transmission while claiming an SIR-style model is invalid

rules.name: Replicator dynamics seed
rules.input_form: population of strategies with payoff-dependent updates
preconditions: Strategy shares and payoff functions are fixed
rules.operation: Evolve population shares by payoff advantage relative to the population average.
examples: Strategies with above-average payoff increase share while below-average strategies decline in a competitive population model
counterexamples: Changing shares with no payoff-relative update structure is not automatically replicator dynamics

rules.name: Stochastic volatility seed
rules.input_form: asset-price model with evolving latent volatility state
preconditions: A diffusion-based asset model and stochastic volatility state are fixed
rules.operation: Couple asset-price evolution to a separate stochastic volatility process.
examples: Option-pricing structure can depend on both price uncertainty and volatility dynamics rather than on constant variance alone
counterexamples: Treating every diffusion-pricing model as constant-volatility Black-Scholes is invalid once volatility becomes state-dependent

rules.name: Partition function thermodynamic seed
rules.input_form: equilibrium ensemble with microscopic state-sum structure
preconditions: A standard equilibrium ensemble and temperature scale are fixed
rules.operation: Recover macroscopic thermodynamic quantities from partition-function structure.
examples: Free energy, entropy, and response quantities can be recovered from one partition-function object rather than by separate unrelated formulas
counterexamples: Arbitrary state weights without normalization and temperature structure are not automatically partition-function models

rules.name: Fluctuation response seed
rules.input_form: equilibrium observable fluctuations with weak perturbation data
preconditions: An equilibrium ensemble and weak-response regime are fixed
rules.operation: Relate equilibrium fluctuations to linear response in the standard statistical-mechanics regime.
examples: Observable variance can predict weak-response behavior near equilibrium instead of requiring a fully separate model
counterexamples: Strong nonequilibrium response does not automatically satisfy equilibrium fluctuation-response relations

rules.name: Hydrostatic balance seed
rules.input_form: large-scale atmospheric or oceanic vertical momentum structure
preconditions: A large-scale geophysical flow regime and gravity field are fixed
rules.operation: Reduce vertical momentum structure to hydrostatic pressure-gravity balance when the standard regime applies.
examples: Large-scale atmospheric and oceanic models often reduce vertical momentum structure to pressure-gravity balance
counterexamples: Rapidly accelerating vertical flows are not automatically hydrostatic

rules.name: Geostrophic balance seed
rules.input_form: rotating large-scale flow with horizontal pressure-gradient data
preconditions: A rotating-frame geophysical model and large-scale regime are fixed
rules.operation: Balance Coriolis and horizontal pressure-gradient forces in the standard geostrophic regime.
examples: Synoptic-scale atmospheric motion is often approximated through pressure-Coriolis balance rather than full acceleration terms
counterexamples: Small-scale or highly ageostrophic flows are not automatically geostrophic

rules.name: Reaction network conservation seed
rules.input_form: reaction network with stoichiometric matrix
preconditions: A reaction network and species-balance interpretation are fixed
rules.operation: Constrain chemical trajectories by stoichiometric conservation relations.
examples: Total atom counts or conserved moieties can constrain system trajectories before any numerical solve is attempted
counterexamples: Assuming every concentration can vary independently despite stoichiometric constraints is invalid

rules.name: Chemical equilibrium law seed
rules.input_form: reaction system with forward and reverse equilibrium structure
preconditions: A thermodynamic-kinetic equilibrium setting is fixed
rules.operation: Relate long-time chemical composition to equilibrium-constant structure.
examples: Long-time chemical composition can be constrained by equilibrium-constant structure rather than only by transient kinetics
counterexamples: Applying equilibrium laws unchanged to strongly driven nonequilibrium reactors is invalid

rules.name: Threshold cascade seed
rules.input_form: network diffusion model with local activation thresholds
rules.output_form: cascade condition and adoption spread pattern
preconditions: A graph, threshold rule, and seeded state are fixed
rules.operation: Trigger adoption cascades when local network thresholds are exceeded.
examples: A small seeded minority can generate large adoption if neighborhood thresholds and graph structure align appropriately
counterexamples: Treating every diffusion process as threshold-free independent contagion is invalid

rules.name: Centrality influence seed
rules.input_form: interaction network with candidate influence ranking
preconditions: A graph-mediated interaction model and centrality notion are fixed
rules.operation: Rank influence by structural centrality in the network.
examples: Intervention on a structurally central node may alter diffusion far more than intervention on a peripheral node
counterexamples: Assuming all nodes contribute equally regardless of graph position is invalid

rules.name: Psychometric curve seed
rules.input_form: stimulus intensity and response probability data
preconditions: A discrimination task and stimulus-response setting are fixed
rules.operation: Model response probability as a smooth psychometric transition across stimulus intensity.
examples: Discrimination performance is often modeled by graded threshold behavior rather than by one abrupt binary switch only
counterexamples: A raw accuracy percentage with no stimulus-response structure is not automatically a psychometric curve

rules.name: Drift diffusion decision seed
rules.input_form: sequential evidence stream with noise and decision boundaries
preconditions: An evidence-accumulation setting and decision thresholds are fixed
rules.operation: Model sequential choice through noisy evidence accumulation with absorbing decision boundaries.
examples: Both accuracy and response time can emerge from one evidence-accumulation model rather than from separate unrelated rules
counterexamples: Arbitrary delayed responses do not automatically arise from drift-diffusion evidence accumulation
